segments.text: My grandfather was a man who hardly spoke
He seldom talked about himself
And rarely showed his emotions openly
When I was young, that confused me
What was he thinking?
Did he dislike me?
But as the years passed
I came to understand him
His silence was not coldness
But a quiet love
The generation that lived through the war
He who tends to avoid talking about it
Remembering itself causes pain
They touch the past only briefly
After my grandfather passed away
I found notebooks he had been writing
And them his detailed memories of the battlefield
And his private feelings about his family
Were recorded in small handwriting
He had truly loved us
It was simply difficult for him to put it into words
For him, love was shown through action
Telling the field with me on his day
Or secretly sending a small gift
On his grandchild's birthday
Inside my grandfather's silence
I grasped true kindness
His silence did not mean that words were useless
Rather, there was a love that went beyond words
On my late grandfather's birthday
I go to his grave to offer flowers
I briefly join my hands in prayer
And quietly speak to him for a short time
My grandfather, even now, in an invisible form, lives within my heart.
